additionalCoursework:
Beyond the prerequisites, the most useful courses to take are Physiology, Genetics, and Cell Biology. These courses have some tricky concepts to master and having some familiarity with them ahead of time will be to your benefit once you enter medical school. Microbiology and Immunology may also be helpful. Courses such as Anatomy, Neuroscience, Histology, Pathology, and Pharmacology generally are subjects that can be fairly easily mastered once you enter medical school but take them as an undergrad if you enjoy them.

When it comes to suggestions of what non-science courses you can take, we recommend Psychology courses addressing the cognitive, abnormal, and developmental aspects of human behavior, knowledge of which will help you in becoming a good physician. Courses related to public health, ethics, communication skills are also of increasing benefit, as doctors become more sophisticated in these areas.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
The Norton College of Medicine (COM) of Upstate Medical University commits to creating and sustaining an environment that is equitable, respectful, and free from prejudice for students, faculty, staff, patients, families, and members of our community.

It is our policy to promote a diverse and inclusive campus, through the recruitment of faculty, staff, and students, admissions initiatives, and support programs. We are committed to addressing the shortage of doctors in small communities and rural areas in our region, and in urban underserved communities. We promote the values of diversity and inclusion throughout the mission of the university and in the various functions supporting those missions. Diversity adds value to the learning environment of our students, and we believe it will enhance their commitment to addressing inequities in healthcare.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Students must formally request a leave of absence.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: The Campus Activities staff works to coordinate a diverse (social, cultural and recreational) co-curricular activities program for the Upstate community. They advise and assist more than 65 student organizations, produce a comprehensive intramural sports program that boasts over 9 sports, operates the CAB fitness and athletic facilities and coordinates on-going programs for Upstate students, faculty and staff. In addition, the Director of Campus Activities and Special Projects also advises the Student Government and the Campus Activities Governing Board.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: Located in Syracuse, New York's fourth-largest city, SUNY Upstate is a compact, easy-to-navigate campus. We have a new human anatomy lab, an excellent library, and a teaching hospital that is connected to our main academic building. Syracuse is an affordable, medium-sized city with big-city sports, arts, and recreation. Just outside the city, you will find numerous parks, lakes, mountains, golf courses, ski slopes, hiking trails, and beaches.  University Hospital is a level-one trauma center and tertiary care hospital that services 21 different counties.
medSchoolStudLife.housing:
Geneva Tower provides housing to students from all four colleges at SUNY Upstate Medical University. Offering fully-furnished standard rooms, studio apartments, one and two-bedroom apartments, and four-bedroom suites. For more information, please see http://www.upstate.edu/currentstudents/campuslife/residence/
Due to its convenient location and the availability of many amenities, we would strongly encourage students to live in our on-campus housing option.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Spectrum is SUNY Upstate's LGBTQIA+ club that promotes inclusion among students and faculty. We strive to create spaces for people of all identities to feel safe. We also host events to raise awareness of healthcare issues that are particularly relevant to the LGBTQIA+ community.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: Student Disability Support Services serves as the coordinator of educational services for students with disabilities. Requests for physical and programmatic accommodations at the Upstate Medical University, as they relate to the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, are coordinated through this office.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Professional attire and white coat in clinical settings.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Academic Support Services facilitates student success in the classroom by offering a variety of services and programs. Services provided include workshops, academic counseling and peer tutoring.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Patient interaction begins in the first month of the first year
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Mixture of lecture-based & active learning sessions, with student response, team-based learning, small group discussions, simulation experiences, standardized patients, lab work, and online modules.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Required block and longitudinal clerkships begin in the fourth semester. Final three semesters consist of acting internships, electives including basic science selective, and residency prep course.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: MEDSET is an intense 4-week program designed to expose students to the rigors of medical school. It exposes students to the curriculum of the first year and provides a solid foundation.
medSchoolCurriculum.rankStudents: Yes at the end of the third year
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Attendance is not required for most pre-clinical lectures. They are recorded for later viewing. Small group and some other sessions are mandatory. Core clerkship lectures are mandatory.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: A newly revised curriculum integrates foundational, clinical, and health systems sciences and provides early clinical exposure, and offers individualized educational options. The pre-clerkship three semesters include organ-based units co-directed by basic science and clinical faculty and a concurrent longitudinal clinical course with outpatient and inpatient experiences. Active and small group learning built around clinical cases are featured. During the clerkship year, students complete 45 weeks of core clinical rotations and have five weeks of elective time. Throughout the curriculum, students participate in standardized patient, interprofessional, simulation, and community engagement experiences. Intersessions focus on health systems science topics including social determinants of health, health system improvement, ethics and legal issues, and leadership. An accelerated MD pathway, rural medicine program, research opportunities, microcredentials, and combined degrees are offered.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: SUNY Upstate Medical University is committed to educating physicians who are likely to practice primary care in small and/or rural communities in its region. The Rural Medical Scholars Program provides additional support for students who want to practice medicine in the state’s underserved areas in an effort to address the shortage of doctors in those communities.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Upstate offers a formal MD/Ph.D. program for those that are interested. We also offer opportunities for students to obtain research experience throughout their medical education if they so choose.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Upstate Medical University Hospital, Upstate University Hospital at Community General, St. Joseph's Hospital Health Center of Syracuse, and Crouse-Irving Memorial Hospital
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Pass/Fail in the first 2 years; Honors/High Pass/Pass in 3rd and 4th years

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The College of Medicine was established in 1834 as the Geneva Medical College. The college was transferred to the State University of New York (SUNY) system in 1950. In 1999, its name changed to SUNY Upstate Medical University to best reflect the college's academic mission in medical care, research, and education. In 2021, the College of Medicine was named The Alan and Marlene Norton College of Medicine. Dr. Alan Norton was a 1966 graduate of Upstate Medical University.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: The primary mission of SUNY Upstate is the education of health professionals and biomedical research. Upstate's clinical faculty and healthcare professionals commit themselves to education and patient care, demonstrating excellence and compassion. In pursuing its mission, Upstate provides its faculty, staff, students, and volunteers an environment of mutual trust and respect, with opportunities to grow personally and professionally and to make a positive difference in the lives of others.
medSchoolInformation.programAbout: These programs are tailored for aspiring medical professionals, providing a seamless transition from both Binghamton University and Syracuse University to Upstate’s Norton College of Medicine. Students selected for the BS/MD Program will experience collateral and co-curricular support for their medical school aspirations, along with mentorship opportunities and early faculty-student interaction with Upstate’s Norton College of Medicine faculty. The BS/MD program is highly competitive, offering up to five annual places each for Binghamton pre-medical students and Syracuse high school seniors.

medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: While we prefer a committee letter, we also accept letters from science faculty, supervisors, and clinical professionals you have worked with.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Interviews are conducted on select Mondays, Tuesdays, and Wednesdays beginning in September and continue until early March. In addition to the interview sessions, applicants will participate in a Meet & Greet with admissions staff and current medical students. On-campus applicant events will be held in the Spring and applicants will have the opportunity to get a feel for the medical school, tour the facilities, learn more about the medical school offerings, and interact with faculty, students, and staff.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Interviews are conducted virtually using an MMI interview format. Applicants will interview with students, faculty, administrators, or community physicians.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
**Response to COVID-19 - Information for 2026 Admissions Cycle** 

Pass/Fail Coursework - If your undergraduate institution required students to move to Pass/Fail coursework during the pandemic, we will accept this. We also suggest that if you took a Pass/Fail in a prerequisite course that you take an additional upper-level science course to demonstrate additional competency in the subject area. 

Because of the impact of COVID on the availability of in-person courses, SUNY Upstate Medical University will consider on-line science prerequisite courses, including courses in which students received a grade of Pass/Fail, taken during the 2020 and 2021 academic years.

Outside of these years, courses need to be completed in person for a letter grade.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: We consider the most recent MCAT scores.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: We do not have a minimum undergraduate GPA used to consider post-bacc or graduate-level course work. If students have taken additional coursework, it will be considered.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: We would consider a minimum of 15 credit hours of additional coursework should an applicant's undergraduate GPA be of concern.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Community College coursework shall be considered based on student's overall record. If a student is matriculated at an accredited four-year college or university, the Admissions Committee strongly recommends that all science prerequisites be completed at that institution. If a student begins college at an accredited two-year college and transfers to a competitive four-year college or university to complete their bachelor's degree, they must demonstrate continued academic excellence in any remaining prerequisite and/or upper-level science courses taken at the four-year institution.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Information should be uploaded via the applicant portal.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: The Norton College of Medicine at Upstate Medical University strives to select students who possess the intelligence, integrity and personal and emotional characteristics considered necessary to become effective physicians. Admitted students should have the intellectual and physical abilities to acquire the knowledge, behaviors and skills taught in the curriculum, all of which are necessary for graduate medical training in a variety of disciplines.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Accepted applicants who are US citizens or permanent residents are eligible to apply for financial aid. The Financial Aid Office generally sends out financial aid award letters beginning in January.
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: The Office of Financial Aid provides financial assistance to students whose personal and family resources are not adequate to cover the expenses involved in attending SUNY Upstate Medical University. Financial assistance is provided through loans, grants, scholarships, and student employment.

medSchoolPrograms.name: Upstate Medical University offers the Master of Public Health. The MPH is a professional degree which provides a population-based perspective and is designed to prepare students to investigate and manage public health problems.
medSchoolPrograms.deadline: At the point of AMCAS submission

medSchoolPrograms.info: The MedPrep Academic Enhancement MS in Medical Technology provides a one-year course of study designed to help college graduates strengthen their academic credentials to apply to medical school.  Through this program, students endure a rigorous didactic curriculum to demonstrate academic preparedness for medical school.  Acceptance into this program also guarantees an admission interview with our medical school.

MD/MPH 
This program provides students with a comprehensive and integrative approach to medical and public health education, preparing graduates to address complex health challenges facing communities locally, nationally, and globally. The MD/MPH typically takes about five years to earn both degrees. 

MD/MBA
Upstate Medical University and Syracuse University have partnered to provide a dual-degree MD/MBA program. This five-year program provides graduates with the unique training and experiences as physicians to navigate the business realms of healthcare and healthcare administration. 

MD/Ph.D.
Our MD/Ph.D. program trains future physician-scientists who, by combining the practice of medicine in the clinic with biomedical research in the laboratory, are uniquely qualified to bring the power of modern science to our understanding and treatment of human disease.

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: Accepted students must "commit to enroll" no later than 21 days prior to the start of our Orientation program.

medSchoolMdPathway.programDesc: Upstate Medical University's Norton College of Medicine three-year MD program (3YP) is for high-performing students who want to be on a directed pathway to a residency at SUNY Upstate Medical University or UHS in Binghamton.  Following their medical school acceptance, students may apply to the program.  Acceptance into this program leads to a directed pathway to a designated residency at SUNY Upstate Medical University or UHS in Binghamton.
medSchoolMdPathway.residencyAffiliationPathway: Directed residency option for all Three-Year MD students

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistInformation: This number varies from year to year.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: Upstate requires Biochemistry in place of Organic Chemistry II and Statistics in place of Calculus.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: Prerequisites should not be older than 10 years.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: The Admissions Committee takes an applicant's total qualifications into consideration for the study and practice of medicine. Major factors in the selection of applicants include a review of college records, MCAT scores, letters of recommendation, experiences, personal interviews, communication skills, character, and motivation.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: No set number of shadowing hours but hands-on clinical experience is strongly recommended.
